video_title: Owner Ryan Smith on Jazz Taking Darryn Peterson & Why All NBA News is SO WRONG

quotes.speaker: Ryan Smith
quotes.summary_phrase: Ryan Smith on the Jazz drafting Darryn Peterson with the second pick
quotes.excerpt: getting the second draft spot was something we needed in Utah.
quotes.quote: It was good. I like the draft, I like where we end up. We're super excited in Utah about DP. I thought Danny, Austin, Will, I thought they did a really good job in coming together. Look, you need a little bit of luck in the NBA and getting the second draft spot was something we needed in Utah.

quotes.speaker: Ryan Smith
quotes.summary_phrase: Ryan Smith on the Jazz's draft strategy and Darryn Peterson's fit
quotes.excerpt: Darryn Peterson was definitely the number one pick for most of the year.
quotes.quote: If you look at the last maybe three out of the last six years and maybe possibly the years going forward, you basically had three number one picks there all at different positions. So I think it was Danny's choice on how you wanted to go. Darryn Peterson was definitely the number one pick for most of the year. And then as we got into it, we were in a pretty good spot. So we liked it. We love Darryn, we love what he can do. He slides in perfectly next to Keyonte and if you look at adding Daron Holmes II, that was probably pretty fortuitous on timing.

quotes.speaker: Ryan Smith
quotes.summary_phrase: Ryan Smith on the Jazz's relationship with the Boozer family
quotes.excerpt: Carlos has been such a -- it's been an interesting process because he's got this confidence about his boy.
quotes.quote: Danny's got 47 years in the league and if you count how many of those types of conversations he's had, it's pretty crazy. To be honest with you, I love everything about the Boozer family. Carlos has been such a -- it's been an interesting process because he's got this confidence about his boy, but his boy stands alone. Anyone who's met Cameron Boozer, he's a contagious personality and I loved our conversations with him. He's going to be fine wherever he ends up and I think they all know that. He was the youngest player in the draft, but he's going to be a veteran on whatever team he shows up on on day one.

quotes.speaker: Ryan Smith
quotes.summary_phrase: Ryan Smith on the Jazz's roster construction and Darryn Peterson's maturity
quotes.excerpt: Darryn's got some great youth around him to play hard and energy, but also some veterans in there.
quotes.quote: We definitely have a centerpiece. If you look at our roster with Ace Bailey, Keyonte, Walker, and then you kind of have a little bit more veteran approach with Jaren and Lowry, who were just two of the greatest dudes, you're in this unique timeline spot where it's like, whoa, we have a little bit of everything coming together. And I think Darryn's got some great youth around him to play hard and energy, but also some veterans in there that can teach him how to be. But he's a mature kid. I think he's pretty misunderstood. You go back through and look at the interviews, how he's handled his media, everything there, he knows what's up, he knows what the narrative is around it.

quotes.speaker: Ryan Smith
quotes.summary_phrase: Ryan Smith on his collaborative approach to Jazz front-office decisions
quotes.excerpt: I'm just more of a feel player. There's stuff I care about and there's stuff that Austin cares about.
quotes.quote: Being in this position, if I look over my career and I'm somewhat on the younger side from an age standpoint of owners, but for me it's all about the team and the nucleus that we're putting together, which includes me and Will and Austin and Danny. That's our group and I got to be a team player and they got to be a team player. I'm just more of a feel player. There's stuff I care about and there's stuff that Austin cares about. But what matters is that we're locked in and we're locked in together. There's no ego in our room, which is actually really, really cool.

quotes.speaker: Ryan Smith
quotes.summary_phrase: Ryan Smith on the prevalence of misinformation in NBA reporting
quotes.excerpt: I've never been in a business where so much is untrue that's out there.
quotes.quote: There's reasons why those narratives take off and the one thing in the NBA is a lot of times I think we all have to do this, we all have to sit back and be like, okay, that's out there. I've never been in a business where so much is untrue that's out there. It's just completely untrue. And then you've got like your mother-in-law reading, can you believe this? And I'm like, oh my word. Like it's just -- and I try to explain to other consumers of regular news out there in the world, I was like, hey, if the rest of the world's anything like the NBA that's out there and how much is untrue, that's sad.

quotes.speaker: Ryan Smith
quotes.summary_phrase: Ryan Smith on the reality of NBA pre-draft workouts
quotes.excerpt: I don't even call it a workout. I call it dinner.
quotes.quote: We met with Darryn at the combine. Darryn was awesome in the interview. Darryn wanted to go number one. Everyone wants to go number one. But by the way, we had three different top guys come in. I don't even call it a workout. I call it dinner. I don't even go. I'm like, okay, I'll go to dinner with you because there's no sweat, there's no nothing. They're sitting down with Will watching film. They put on their jersey to check out the size and everything. They take a couple of pictures, they call it a workout, but no one's doing like the three-minute run to see how fast they can go up and down the court.

quotes.speaker: Ryan Smith
quotes.summary_phrase: Ryan Smith on the Jazz's outlook for the upcoming season
quotes.excerpt: I don't want to set expectations, but like we need to start winning.
quotes.quote: I don't want to set expectations, but like we need to start winning. I think that's that's that's kind of where we're at. When we took over, I took over what was the number one team in the regular season and we got, I mean, it was interesting. My first day was like post-COVID. We were kind of into COVID and I had like two weeks to get a deal done with Rudy Gobert and Donovan Mitchell. It was really complicated because normally you have a long time to do this, but that team came out, we were number one in the regular season the first year and just got bounced early.

quotes.speaker: Ryan Smith
quotes.summary_phrase: Ryan Smith on Walker Kessler's role with the Jazz
quotes.excerpt: We love Walk. He's a big piece of what we're going.
quotes.quote: We love Walk. He's a big piece of what we're going.
